partners.diseaseBName: syndromic X-linked intellectual disability Raymond type
partners.mechanism_chain: MGAT2 (HGNC:7440) —DISRUPTS→ N-glycosylation initiation (GO:0006486); N-glycosylation initiation (GO:0006486) —DECREASES→ GlcNAc-containing precursors (CHEBI:59835); GlcNAc-containing precursors (CHEBI:59835) —DECREASES→ GM1 ganglioside biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-194279); GM1 ganglioside biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-194279) —DECREASES→ GM1 ganglioside (CHEBI:17620); GM1 ganglioside (CHEBI:17620) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); GM1 ganglioside (CHEBI:17620) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital disorder of glycosylation (HP:0030722); ZDHHC9 (HGNC:24073) —DISRUPTS→ GM1 ganglioside biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-194279); GM1 ganglioside biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-194279) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); GM1 ganglioside biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-194279) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital disorder of glycosylation (HP:0030722). Mutations in MGAT2 impair the initiation of N-glycosylation, leading to a reduction in GlcNAc-containing precursors necessary for complex glycan synthesis. Concurrently, mutations in ZDHHC9 disrupt protein palmitoylation, which is essential for the proper function of enzymes involved in ganglioside biosynthesis, including those in the GM1 ganglioside pathway. Both pathways converge on the biosynthesis of GM1 gangliosides, and a deficiency in functional GM1 gangliosides leads to intellectual disability and is a hallmark of congenital disorders of glycosylation.

partners.mechanism_chain: MGAT2 (HGNC:7024) —DISRUPTS→ N-linked glycosylation initiation (GO:0006486); N-linked glycosylation initiation (GO:0006486) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital disorder of glycosylation (MONDO:0008908); PRKCSH (HGNC:9345) —DISRUPTS→ Oligosaccharyltransferase (OST) complex activity (GO:0005797); Oligosaccharyltransferase (OST) complex activity (GO:0005797) —DISRUPTS→ Biliary epithelial cell function and bile duct development (GO:0001702); N-linked glycosylation initiation (GO:0006486) —DISRUPTS→ Biliary epithelial cell function and bile duct development (GO:0001702); Biliary epithelial cell function and bile duct development (GO:0001702) —LEADS_TO→ Polycystic liver disease 1 (MONDO:0008265). Both MGAT2-CDG and PCLD1 converge on the disruption of normal biliary epithelial cell function and bile duct development (GO:0001702). MGAT2 mutations impair N-linked glycosylation initiation (GO:0006486), a process essential for proper protein folding and function within the endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi. PRKCSH mutations disrupt the activity of the Oligosaccharyltransferase (OST) complex (GO:0005797), which is also critical for initiating N-linked glycosylation. The downstream consequence of impaired glycosylation and OST complex function affects the structure and function of biliary epithelial cells, ultimately leading to the cystic phenotype observed in polycystic liver disease and the systemic glycosylation defects in CDG.
